headline: New law requires the IRS to explain math and clerical error notices more clearly and offer more ways to dispute them.
what_it_does: When the IRS finds a math or clerical error on a tax return, its notice must now describe the error, name the specific return line, show an itemized calculation of the changes, give a phone number for the automated transcript service, and state the deadline to ask for the extra tax to be removed (an "abatement"). The IRS must also send a clear notice when it removes tax charged because of such an error. It must let people request an abatement in writing, online, by phone, or in person. The IRS must also test sending these notices by certified or registered mail and report the results to Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Taxpayers who get IRS math or clerical error notices
who_it_affects.how: They will receive notices that spell out what the error was, where it was on the return, how the tax was recalculated, and the deadline to challenge it.

who_it_affects.group: Taxpayers who want to challenge extra tax from a math or clerical error
who_it_affects.how: They will be able to request that the tax be removed in writing, electronically, by phone, or in person.
It must change its notices, set up abatement request procedures, run a certified or registered mail pilot program, and report to Congress on that pilot.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 25, 2025; the summary does not state specific start dates for each requirement.
